# Security Checklist: ISK-0008 — Local Developer Environment & Reproducible Compose

**Purpose**: Check that the requirements for environment safety, generated passwords, published ports, image hardening, supply chain, and reset scope are complete, clear, and traceable to the threat model
**Created**: 2026-11-17
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Environment Safety

- [x] CHK001 - Is every development-only value the topology needs listed by field, with the overlay named as its only location? [Completeness, Spec §TR-8, §FR-011, Contract §Documents 3]
- [x] CHK002 - Is it stated why the Redis endpoint and primitive selections sit in the overlay, although selections are not development-only? [Clarity, Research R5]
- [x] CHK003 - Is the base document's validity defined measurably: alone, with no environment name, as production-grade? [Measurability, Spec §FR-012, §SC-007, Contract §Documents 2]
- [x] CHK004 - Are the error codes for overlay values outside `development` named, so that a test can assert them? [Measurability, Data model §Plane configuration documents]
- [x] CHK005 - Is it specified that each plane sets `ISKENDER_ENVIRONMENT=development` itself, so a developer's shell value never reaches a container, and that no other Iskender variable is passed in? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases, Contract §Documents 1]
- [x] CHK006 - Is the asymmetry of which plane rejects which document recorded as a correction, with the reason the control-plane documents are still kept apart? [Consistency, Spec §US3.6, Research R6]

## Passwords

- [x] CHK007 - Are the password source, length, alphabet, file location, and file and directory modes all specified? [Completeness, Spec §TR-6, §FR-008, Contract §Passwords 1]
- [x] CHK008 - Is the set of places where a password must never appear defined the same way in the spec, the contract, and the smoke assertions? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, §SC-004, Contract §Passwords 4, §Smoke assertions 7]
- [x] CHK009 - Is the provisioning script's handling of passwords defined so that none appears on a command line, in SQL text, or in an error echo? [Gap, Contract §PostgreSQL 2, Research R7]
  - Settled in `checklist`: research R7 and T017 passed each password to `psql` with `-v name=value`, which puts it on `psql`'s command line, although the contract said "never on a command line". The contract, R7, and T017 now read them with `\getenv` and set `VERBOSITY terse` and `log_min_error_statement` to `panic` for the session, so a failed statement is never echoed with its text.
- [x] CHK010 - Is the smoke value search defined so that the values it searches for are never command-line arguments? [Gap, Contract §Smoke assertions 7, Research R13]
  - Settled in `checklist`: R13 and T030 searched with `grep -F` and named no way to give the values, which in practice means `grep -F "$value"`, visible to any process listing. The contract, R13, and T030 now give the values through a pattern file descriptor (`grep -F -f` with a process substitution written by the `printf` builtin).
- [x] CHK011 - Is the behavior defined for a password file that exists but is incomplete, malformed, or has lost its owner-only mode? [Edge Case, Gap, Contract §Passwords 2]
  - Settled in `checklist`: only an absent file was defined. The contract, R8, the data model, T019, and T035 now say that a file without exactly the three names and 32-character values makes start exit 2, naming the reset script and changing nothing, and that every start sets the modes to `0700` and `0600` again. Exit code 2 already covers an unusable prerequisite.
- [x] CHK012 - Is the risk of passwords in the `postgres` container's environment recorded as a known limit, with why it gives no reader anything new? [Assumption, Contract §Known limits, Research R8]
- [x] CHK013 - Is the rejected alternative of Compose `secrets` recorded with the concrete reason it fails? [Traceability, Research R8]

## Ports and Reachability

- [x] CHK014 - Is every published port listed with its host address, default, override variable, and mode, and is "nothing else is published" stated? [Completeness, Spec §FR-015, Contract §Ports]
- [x] CHK015 - Is "no health port is ever published" stated for every mode, and is the in-network probe specified so that smoke never needs one? [Consistency, Spec §TR-9, §TR-14, Contract §Ports 1, §Services]
- [x] CHK016 - Is the one place where a local run is reachable from the network, a native host on all interfaces, recorded as a known limit? [Coverage, Contract §Native runs 4, §Known limits]
- [x] CHK017 - Is Valkey's `--protected-mode no` justified, with the networks it is reachable on in each mode? [Clarity, Research R15, Contract §Valkey]

## Hardening and Supply Chain

- [x] CHK018 - Are the plane, migration, and probe services' hardening settings listed, including what may not be set? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, Contract §Hardening 1]
- [x] CHK019 - Is the exception for `postgres` and `valkey`, which keep their images' own users, stated with its reason and its compensating control? [Clarity, Research R4, Contract §Hardening 4]
- [x] CHK020 - Is every image pinned by digest, with the rule for changing a digest, and is the probe image's licence validated with its evidence? [Completeness, Spec §TR-4, §AV-4, Contract §Services 1, Research R14]
- [x] CHK021 - Is the build context protected from carrying the password file, without changing either Dockerfile? [Gap, Contract §Layout 3, Research R1]
- [x] CHK022 - Is the user-level proxy feed excluded from every committed file? [Coverage, Plan §Constraints]

## Reset Scope

- [x] CHK023 - Is reset's scope defined by the validated project name, with ISK-0007's project names shown never to match? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020, Contract §Project name 2]
- [x] CHK024 - Are pattern-based removal, image removal, and removal outside `local/` excluded explicitly? [Completeness, Spec §TR-15, Contract §Scripts]
- [x] CHK025 - Is the confirmation rule defined for an interactive shell, a non-interactive shell, and a declined answer? [Edge Case, Spec §US4.4, Contract §Scripts]
  - Settled in `checklist`: the exit code for a declined answer was only in T013. The contract and R12 now state that any answer other than `y` or `Y` removes nothing and exits 0.
- [x] CHK026 - Is the case of two checkouts on one Docker host under the same project name addressed, given that a reset from either reaches the other's data? [Edge Case, Gap, Contract §Project name 4]
  - Settled in `checklist`: the spec assumes one topology per checkout, and the contract allowed several projects only from one checkout. The contract now states that the name is per Docker host, so each checkout that runs its own topology sets its own `ISKENDER_LOCAL_PROJECT`, records this as a known limit, and T040 puts it in the guide. This documents the existing rule and adds no behavior.

## Threat Model

- [x] CHK027 - Does each row of the spec's Negative Security and Failure Scenarios table map to a contract rule and a test? [Traceability, Spec §Negative Security and Failure Scenarios, Contract §Threat model]
- [x] CHK028 - Is the out-of-scope boundary for fabricated secrets, interim credential providers, and TLS between local services stated? [Completeness, Spec §Out of Scope]
